paras: The shooting of Coot Miles took place on August 9, 1900, in Phoenix City (also spelled Phenix City), Alabama, when Policeman John Moon shot Miles, a Black man, as he ran from an attempted arrest. Miles was hit in the lung at a distance of about 175 yards and was described as probably mortally wounded, though he was still alive that night. A Columbus, Georgia, dispatch carried the story to Birmingham and Savannah papers, one of which called Miles a "negro desperado."

According to the dispatch, Miles was wanted on three warrants in Phoenix City and neighboring Girard, one of them for grand larceny. It was "said," without a named source, that he had threatened local officers' lives and carried a gun for them. The Savannah Morning News added that Miles was the son of a "negro desperado" who had recently escaped from Phenix City officers.

When Officer Moon saw Miles, he started to arrest him, and Miles ran. Moon gave chase and fired as he went, using, in the Savannah version, "a big Colt's revolver." The fifth shot struck Miles, who ran into a nearby ravine, where Moon found him shot through the lung. Neither report describes Miles firing or drawing a weapon during the chase.
Miles was "still lingering" on the night of the shooting, according to the Birmingham paper. No later report of his death, an inquest, or an inquiry appears in the coverage.

The only coverage found is one Columbus dispatch, printed on August 10 by the Birmingham Age-Herald and the Savannah Morning News. The Age-Herald ran it as a "Special" under the headline "Negro Fatally Wounded," with the deck "Ran from the Officers and Was Shot Down." The Savannah Morning News chose "Desperado Fatally Shot," opened by calling Miles "a negro desperado," and closed by linking him to his father's reputation.

Both papers presented the officer's account as fact, while attributing the claim of threats only to what "is said." Both headlines called the wound fatal even though the text said Miles was still alive. No Black-press coverage of the shooting was found.

reader.title: Shooting of Coot Miles
bases: A single policeman, John Moon, shot Miles while trying to arrest him on outstanding warrants; no crowd or posse is mentioned (A1, A2).
Both articles print the same Columbus, Ga. dispatch of August 9 nearly word for word, so they are one report, not two independent ones (A1, A2).

accounts.label: Columbus, Ga. dispatch (officers' version)
accounts.gist: Miles, wanted on three warrants and said to have threatened officers, ran when Moon moved to arrest him; Moon fired as he chased him, and the fifth shot hit Miles 175 yards away.

framing.detail: The Age-Herald ran the Columbus special under 'Negro Fatally Wounded / Ran from the Officers and Was Shot Down', with no comment.
The Savannah Morning News headlined 'Desperado Fatally Shot', called Miles a 'negro desperado' and tied him to a 'negro desperado' father.

sources.note: Columbus, Ga. special of Aug. 9, 'Negro Fatally Wounded': Policeman John Moon shot fleeing 'Coot' Miles in Phoenix City; shot through the lung, still lingering that night.
quotes: "Coot" Miles, a negro, was fatally shot in Phoenix City, Ala., today by Policeman John Moon.
It is said he threatened the life of Phoenix and Girard officers and carried a gun for them.
The fifth shot struck the negro, and he darted into a ravine near by, where the officer found him, shot through the lung and probably mortally wounded.
